INDEPENDENT BASELINE: FINITE-TRACIAL EXPOSURE AND AUXILIARY COMPRESSION
Worker algebra_proof_recon; Sol/max; no descendants; 2026-10-09.
Companion to MASS_REFEREE_LAW_BRIDGE_BASELINE.txt.

STATUS AND PROVENANCE
The old OpenAI 01-operators.tex and 02-exposure.tex were designated
permissible source material. Their complete relevant proofs were read,
and the finite-tracial construction is reconstructed here rather than
assuming their tensor-model scope automatically extends. No new QMS or
sibling bridge proof was read. All source claims remain source-reported
unless proved below. In particular a finite algebra is not a finite
matrix algebra; continuous effect spectrum and nonclosed ranges occur.

Exact source pins, version/read scopes, the SUPPLIED sampler and ACCEPTED
Lin density are in SOURCE_PINS.json and the companion. The endpoint is
conditional on precisely those two supplied inputs, not on a source
parallel-repetition theorem. This document is not externally certified.

1. MODEL AND FIXED EXPOSURE

Let (M,tr) be a finite von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial
state. Let sigma in M be positive, bounded, tr(sigma^2)=1. The state
vector is sigma in L2(M,tr). Alice has left POVMs M_xvec^avec in M and
Bob right POVMs R(N_yvec^bvec), N_yvec^bvec in M. Define

  chi(A,B)=tr(sigma A sigma B).

For positive A,B this is positive, and chi(I,H)<=1 for H<=I. Products
of left/right representations commute even when A,B do not commute in M.

Fix the proper tested set C, event E, probability p>0, m live positions,
d_C=d^|C| and L=log(d_C/p). Relabel live positions in one FIXED order.
The flags are Omega_j=(X_C,Y_C,X_<=j,Y_>j), 0<=j<=m. Given any flag,
full Alice and Bob question strings are independent under the ORIGINAL
question law mu^k: at every live position one question is fixed and the
opposite one has its conditional mu-law, independently between positions.

For tested answer strings alpha,gamma, coarse-grain their POVM effects.
Set F_j^alpha=E[M_Xvec^alpha|Omega_j], H_j^gamma=E[N_Yvec^gamma|Omega_j].
The testing mask theta(X_C,Y_C,alpha,gamma) in {0,1} is the product of
the original acceptance predicates on C. For every j,

  E_Omega_j sum_{alpha,gamma} theta chi(F_j^alpha,H_j^gamma)=p. (A1)

All these operator expectations are finite convex combinations indexed
by CLASSICAL questions, not unproved operator conditional expectations.

INDEPENDENT BASELINE: LOCAL POSTERIOR MASS AND REFEREE LAW
Worker algebra_proof_recon; Sol/max; no descendants; 2026-10-09.
No new QMS or sibling mass-bridge proof was read before this baseline.

STATUS
The mass/referee-law lemma below is proved independently. Together with
the independently reconstructed finite-tracial alignment in the companion
file, it proves the requested conditional-coordinate rounding inequality
conditional only on the explicitly SUPPLIED correlation sampler S and
the ACCEPTED Lin finite-table density theorem L. Those two inputs are not
newly proved here. This is internal mathematics, not external or formal
certification, and makes no historical-priority claim. No exponential or
threshold parallel-repetition theorem is asserted by this packet.

The misleading stronger statement Q approximately Q_R tensor mu is
neither assumed nor derived. The histories used by the players depend
on their own questions. A fixed prefix/suffix exposure suffices once this
weaker interface is used. Randomizing exposure is unnecessary here.

1. EXACT ENDPOINT AND TWO SUPPLIED INPUTS

Let G=(X,Y,A,B,mu,V) be any finite two-player game, V in {0,1}; answer
sets are nonempty and d=|A||B|. Let a commuting strategy for G^k be fixed.
Let C be any proper subset of [k], m=k-|C|>=1, and E be winning all
coordinates in C. Suppose p=Pr(E)>0. Define, with natural logarithms,

  tau=(log(1/p)+|C|log d)/m,
  q=(1/m)sum_{i notin C} Pr(win_i | E).

Then, assuming S and L exactly as follows, the internal conclusion is

  q <= omega_co(G) + 4112 tau^(1/4).                         (T)

S (SUPPLIED finite-tracial CORRELATION sampler). In a finite tracial von
Neumann algebra N, take finite families of unit vectors a_s,b_t in
L2(N), fixed local left/right POVMs P_s,Q_t, and any fixed finite joint
law nu of (s,t). Set D=E_nu ||a_s-b_t||_2^2. The correlation evaluated on
a_s with POVMs P_s,Q_t is denoted C^a_{s,t}. For every zeta>0 there is
ONE legal all-input commuting strategy T, with a shared resource fixed
before (s,t), such that

  E_nu dTV(T_{s,t}, C^a_{s,t}) <= 2048 D^(1/4)+zeta.         (S)

Here dTV is half the full l1 distance of answer distributions. Input
families can include arbitrary finite history labels. No pointwise
promise, product-law promise, minimum question atom, or spectral gap is
inserted. This is the precise correlation form used; a guarantee only
about arbi
